chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

He said: I heard him say: A man accompanied me who would delay Maghrib prayer and pray Fajr early in the darkness. I, however, would pray Maghrib when the sun set, and pray Fajr when dawn became clear to me. The man said to me: What prevents you from doing as I do? For indeed the sun rises upon a people before us, and it sets from us while it is still risen upon others beyond.

He said: So I said: It is only incumbent upon us to pray when the sun has set from us and when dawn rises for us. There is nothing incumbent upon us except that, and it is incumbent upon those people to pray when it sets from them.

key_terms.استبان: Became clearly visible; the true dawn (al-fajr al-sadiq) becoming distinct on the horizon
key_terms.وجبت: Has set/descended; a jurisprudential term for the sun having fully set below the horizon
key_terms.يغلس: To pray in the pre-dawn darkness; praying Fajr before true dawn is clearly visible
key_terms.يمسي: To delay until evening; here meaning delaying the Maghrib prayer past its optimal time at sunset

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the correct time for Maghrib and Fajr prayers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates an encounter with a traveling companion who questioned why the Imam prayed Maghrib immediately at sunset and Fajr at dawn, rather than delaying or praying early. The man argued that since the sun is always rising or setting somewhere, the exact moment should not matter. The Imam clarified the fundamental jurisprudential principle that each community's prayer obligation is determined by their own local astronomical signs -- sunset and dawn as observed from their own location -- not by what occurs elsewhere on earth.
word_analysis: and he would pray early/in darkness
